result.title: Bayes-Adaptive MDPs for Rollout Allocation to Enhance GRPO Training
result.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has demonstrated strong performance in LLM post-training. However, it allocates a uniform rollout budget to every training question, ignoring variations in question difficulty. As a result, highly difficult questions may receive too few rollouts to generate informative positive reward signals, limiting their contribution to training, while moderately difficult questions often receive more rollouts than necessary. In this work, we formulate the problem of difficulty-aware rollout budget allocation to maximize training utility under the same total rollout budget as standard GRPO. We propose AdaRoll-GRPO, which reformulates rollout allocation as a sequential decision-making problem and leverages a Bayes-adaptive Markov decision process (MDP) to learn an adaptive allocation policy. The learned policy is computed offline and applied during GRPO training without introducing additional online optimization overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple reasoning datasets and LLM architectures demonstrate that AdaRoll-GRPO consistently improves GRPO training performance under a fixed rollout budget, highlighting the effectiveness of adaptive rollout allocation for GRPO in LLM post-training.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 GRPO 中每题 rollout 预算的分配建模为顺序决策问题，用 Bayes-adaptive MDP 离线学习难度自适应的分配策略 AdaRoll-GRPO，在总预算不变下提升推理训练效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按题目难度动态分配采样预算」的策略学习与离线应用方式，可能可供核查 LVR 中多步 THINK/LOOK 的动态计算分配与 STOP 停止决策，但文中无视觉证据或 latent 状态内容。
